samples.summary: The new `updateTableCell` / `updateBlock` truncated-rows refusal is gated on the *replacement* model, so every writer that replaces a cell/block with content that contains no table-at-cap walks straight past it and still deletes the peer rows the reader never read
samples.evidence:
The gate added in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3021` (`if (hasTableAtNestingCap(cell.blocks, rowDepth)) this.assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows(...)`) and its twin at `yorkie-doc-store.ts:1831` only consult the tree when the *new* model still carries a table at the cap. Out-of-diff callers replace cells/blocks with content that has none:
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1137,1155` — `Doc.mergeCells` resets every covered cell to a single empty paragraph and then `store.updateTableCell(blockId, r, c, ...)` for the whole rectangle. The covered cell's model has no table at the cap, so the guard is never asked, and the cell node in the CRDT — which may hold a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with rows this reader truncated — is replaced whole. The rows a peer wrote are deleted and replicated, which is exactly the outcome the new refusal exists to prevent. (The top-left cell, which *does* get a table-at-cap in its model, is checked against its own path, which holds nothing truncated, so it passes and then writes the table back rowless.)
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1183-1184` — `Doc.splitCell` does the same for restored covered cells.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4177-4185` — the cell-range delete clears cells then `updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)`; a user-intended delete, but it reaches `updateBlock` with the gate false as well, confirming the gate's shape rather than its intent is what decides.
The fix belongs on the new code: the tree check has to be driven by what is at the target path, not by what the caller is about to write (cheap pre-filter could be the old node, not the new model).

samples.summary: Dropping the merge-expansion budget from `normalizeCellRange`'s default makes `Selection.getNormalizedRange` unbounded for callers that neither paint nor write — including a per-keystroke arrow-key path
samples.evidence:
`normalizeCellRange`/`normalizeRange` now default `budgetCells = Infinity` and only `computeSelectionRects` (selection.ts:715) passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`. The new comments justify this by saying every remaining `getNormalizedRange` caller *acts* on the rectangle, but two out-of-diff callers do not:
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3378` — plain Left/Right/Up/Down with a selection collapses it via `getNormalizedRange`, using only `normalized.start`/`end`. This runs on every such keystroke and now pays the unbounded fixed-point expansion (superlinear in a peer-chosen row count) that the budget was introduced to bound.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:501` — `formatSourcePosition()` (format painter, reached from `copyFormat()` at line 467) likewise only reads the ordered rectangle.
Neither writes anything, so the "a short rectangle corrupts a merge" rationale does not apply to them; they get the hang risk with none of the benefit. Fix belongs on the new code (pass a budget from these read-only callers, or keep the default budgeted and opt the writers out).

samples.summary: The new `setHeader`/`setFooter` refusals appear unreachable: the only production callers never pass `hadHeader/hadFooter === true`
samples.evidence: Both new checks require `header && hadHeader` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1015) / `footer && hadFooter` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1060). Grepping every call site of `setHeader(`/`setFooter(` outside the stores finds only `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:221` (`ensureHeader`) and `:234` (`ensureFooter`), both of which call it exclusively when `this._document.header/footer` is undefined — i.e. the insert branch. No component or EditorAPI path calls them at all. So the replace branch these guards protect has no caller today; the guards are inert and will not be exercised by the suite either. Not harmful, but worth knowing before relying on them.

verdict.reason: The guard is shaped exactly as claimed: yorkie-doc-store.ts:3021 and :1833 gate the tree-side `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` (:1748) on a model-side `hasTableAtNestingCap` (:454) applied to the *replacement* content, then replace the node whole via `editByPath` (:3033, :1847). The claimed bypassing callers are present verbatim: document.ts:1137 resets covered cells to a single empty paragraph and :1155 pushes each through `store.updateTableCell`; splitCell repeats it at :1183-1184; text-editor.ts:4177-4185 clears cells and calls `updateBlockDirect`, reaching `updateBlock` with the gate false. In all three the replacement model carries no table at the cap, so the tree is never consulted and a cell/block node that may hold rows this reader truncated is overwritten — the deletion the refusal exists to prevent. The paths are reachable from the editor UI (editor.ts:4374 merge, :4387 split) with `Doc` built over the store (document.ts:248), and no other guard intervenes (withUpdate, :3277-3285, adds none). In-lane for blast radius (new guard with a reachable out-of-diff bypass) and blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:126), `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:205) and `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:265) all default `budgetCells = Infinity`, and a repo-wide grep shows `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` is passed at exactly one site, `computeSelectionRects` (selection.ts:715). `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (selection.ts:905) passes no budget, yet the new comment at selection.ts:254-260 justifies the unbounded default by claiming every such caller acts on (writes) the rectangle. At least one out-of-diff consumer contradicts that: `formatSourcePosition()` (text-editor.ts:499-513) calls `getNormalizedRange` and only reads `rect.start.rowIndex/colIndex` and `normalized.start/end`, writing nothing; it is reachable from `copyFormat()` (text-editor.ts:466-469) via the keydown handler (text-editor.ts:1247) and via `EditorAPI.copyFormat` (editor.ts:3593, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:148). That site now pays the unbounded superlinear merge expansion over a peer-writable table with none of the correctness benefit the budget removal was justified by — a reachable hang risk on a read-only path, which is a behaviour change to a shared symbol whose other consumers were not accounted for (blast-radius lane). I could not find any guard that removes this. The second cited site (text-editor.ts:3375-3385) is weaker: `handleArrowInner` returns early inside the `if (arrowCellInfo)` branch (text-editor.ts:3043-3044, return at 3348) when the caret is in a table cell, and `normalizeRange` only expands when `tableCellRange` is set (selection.ts:268-288), so the per-keystroke framing may be overstated — but that caveat does not refute the finding, which stands on the format-painter site.

finding.summary: The paste path that writes whole table cells (`pasteTableCells`) bypasses the new `capTableNesting` producer guard
finding.evidence: `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1575) routes a clipboard payload to one of two writers: `pasteTableCells(plan.cells)` or `insertBlocks(plan.blocks)`. Only `insertBlocks` was changed to call `capTableNesting(incoming, this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId))` (text-editor.ts:4568-4573). `pasteTableCells` clones the incoming `TableCell`s verbatim into the target cells (text-editor.ts:4716-4718 and 4748-4749) with no depth check, and those cells may hold nested tables: `getSelectedTableCells` copies the real `cell.blocks` (including nested table blocks) into the waffledocs payload, and `deserializeClipboard`'s sanitizer only bounds the *fragment* at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:72,309). Pasting such a cell rectangle into a cell already near the ceiling produces a model past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, which the store then writes as a table with zero rows (silent loss of the pasted content in the CRDT while the local cache still shows it) and which later makes `writeFullDocument`/`writeDocsRoot` refuse the document entirely. The fix belongs at this site (cap the cells' blocks against `doc.tableNestingDepth` of the target cell), not on the new code.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `pasteTableCells` writes clipboard `TableCell`s verbatim with no nesting-depth check, bypassing the cap that `insertBlocks` got. The code does not read that way. `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4706) computes `cellBaseDepth = this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) + (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` at text-editor.ts:4719-4720 and applies `capTableCellsNesting(cloneTableCells([[cells[r][c]]]), cellBaseDepth)` at BOTH write sites: the new-table branch (text-editor.ts:4730-4734) and the in-table branch (text-editor.ts:4765-4769). `capTableCellsNesting` (clipboard.ts:462-473) delegates to `capTableNesting` (clipboard.ts:429-447), which drops tables at/past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` and substitutes an empty block — the same ceiling the block path enforces. The lines the finding cites as the unguarded clones (4716-4718, 4748-4749) are actually the explanatory comment and the `tableBlockId`/`td` lookup. A repo-wide grep shows `pasteTableCells` has exactly one caller (applyPastePlan, text-editor.ts:1575), so there is no alternate entry point to the cell writer either. The described bypass is not present.

finding.summary: The bounded merge expansion in `normalizeCellRange` also reaches write paths, contrary to the new doc comment that says only the painter passes a budget
finding.evidence: `selection.ts:214` now always passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` inside `normalizeCellRange`, and `normalizeCellRange` is reached from `Selection.getNormalizedRange` — which is not only the painter. `text-editor.ts:4165-4185` uses `getNormalizedRange(...).tableCellRange` to clear the contents of every selected cell and then `doc.updateBlockDirect`, and `text-editor.ts:4322-4325` (`getSelectedTableCells`, feeding copy/cut) uses the same rectangle. On a table large enough to exhaust the budget these writes act on a partially-expanded rectangle: delete skips cells it used to clear, and cut/copy returns a short rectangle — exactly the 'stopped growing early' outcome the new comment in selection.ts:21-48 says is confined to the render path. Either the budget must not apply to `getNormalizedRange` consumers that write, or the comment's claim is wrong.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `normalizeCellRange` unconditionally applies `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`, so the delete/copy/cut write paths reached via `Selection.getNormalizedRange` act on a partially-expanded rectangle. The code is not as described. `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:202-206) declares `budgetCells = Infinity` and forwards that value at selection.ts:223; the cited line 214 is the column clamp, not a budget pass. A repo-wide grep shows the constant is passed at exactly one call site — `computeSelectionRects` at selection.ts:715 (`normalizeRange(range, layout, MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS)`). `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (selection.ts:901-906) calls `normalizeRange(this.range, layout)` with no budget argument, so every consumer reached through it — the cell-rectangle delete at text-editor.ts:4165-4185 and `getSelectedTableCells` at text-editor.ts:4322 — gets the exact, unbounded expansion. The direct gesture/command callers (text-editor.ts:3324, 3967, 3991; table-merge-context.ts:53) likewise use the 2-arg form and default to Infinity. The doc comments at selection.ts:20-52 and 254-260 therefore describe the code accurately, and no write path is budget-limited.
